question: Two events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A)=\frac12$, $P(B)=\frac13$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac23$. Examine whether $A$ and $B$ are independent. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Step 1: Determination of the intersection probability
Using the relation $$P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B),$$ we obtain $$\frac23=\frac12+\frac13-P(A\cap B).$$
Step 2: Simplification
Therefore, $$P(A\cap B)=\frac12+\frac13-\frac23=\frac16.$$
Step 3: Independence criterion
Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent if $$P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B).$$ Here, $$P(A)P(B)=\frac12\times\frac13=\frac16.$$
Step 4: Comparison
We have $$P(A\cap B)=\frac16=P(A)P(B).$$ Thus, the required independence condition is satisfied.
Step 5: Conclusion
Hence, the given events $A$ and $B$ are $$\boxed{\text{independent}}.$$

options.B: $A$ and $B$ are not independent because $P(A\cap B)=\frac{1}{6}\neq P(A)P(B)$
options.C: $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive because $P(A\cap B)=0$
